findings.claim: Row 128's R2 closure note publishes a false coverage claim: 'exercised by every committed table case, all of which run `envelope_shape`' — two of the seven table cases run no envelope_shape check at all.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:128 (HEAD) '… and exercised by every committed table case, all of which run `envelope_shape`'. evals/adversarial/tables-layout-bullet.json and evals/adversarial/tables-cell-div.json have input {"tables": true} and check types ['table','table_markdown','tables_sane'] / ['table','norm_contains','tables_sane'] — no envelope_shape; run_case (src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:507-530) only runs the listed checks. Only 5/7 table cases (aapl-2025-table, msft-2013-table, tgt-2002-table-th, tables-refusal-path, tables-offsets-invariant) run envelope_shape. The same untrue sentence was inherited from the pre-L1 row text ('every committed table case runs both') and restated rather than re-measured.
findings.repro: for f in evals/golden/*table*.json evals/adversarial/tables-*.json; do printf '%s env=%s sane=%s\n' $f $(grep -c envelope_shape $f) $(grep -c tables_sane $f); done
findings.acceptance: Row 128's R2 note (and the `_tables_shape` comment if it is read as a coverage claim) says five of the seven table cases run `envelope_shape` and names the two that run `tables_sane` only — or envelope_shape is added to tables-layout-bullet / tables-cell-div (green, no red-first needed for a tightening already watched red in test_eval_adapter) and the sentence becomes true as written.
